portable_guards: Read numbered bounded chunks, verify the final line, and compare the working file to the exact Git blob.
Materialize foreach output in an array before piping it.
Use the committed owner-manifest contract: exact path coverage, exclusions, and Git-blob identity.
Compute command exit states in separate variables before constructing the object.
Inspect the target, branch, exact head, registration, and surviving process before any retry.
Use short exact filesystem, process, head, branch, and clean-state probes.
Identify the dead-parent child, stop only that owned orphan, then rerun bounded Git plumbing.
Normalize path separators or match the exact worktree basename and branch tuple.
Select top-level counts and bounded rows instead of serializing the whole index.
Promote the array-materialization method as a recurrence guard and use it for every later loop pipeline.
Search directories with rg -g include globs instead of wildcard path arguments.
Delete only the new untracked Vesper scaffolds, retain the failure, and recreate them only after x1 is committed, pushed, clean, and remote-equal.
Replace per-path Git reads with one staged-index map and one git cat-file --batch stream, then regenerate receipts against the same intended x1 scope.
Recheck process existence after inspection and treat an already-exited owned process as quiescent without retrying a stop.
On Windows, express filename selection with rg include globs and keep the searched root literal.
Discover phase-data attribute names read-only before referencing them in an accounting probe.
Validators must distinguish a truthful open route gap from an invalidly promoted workflow instead of requiring every structural workflow request to be fully routable.
Use rg -g for every Windows filename selection, including closeout anchor scans; never pass wildcard path arguments.
